incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: elevated 502/504 rates at API Gateway (edge-gw eu-west-1). Current 5m error rate 18% (baseline ~0.3%). Paging on-call.
Daniel: On it. Paging PD and joining bridge. @Michelle can you grab metrics and recent deploys?
Michelle: grabbing charts — seeing spike start at 08:12 UTC, error type 502 mostly, tail of 504s. Latency also up. Link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/g/edge-gw?from=08:00&to=08:30
Kira: I'm tailing logs on edge-proxy-1/2/3.
Ryan: I see a large increase in upstream connect failures in the proxy logs: "upstream prematurely closed connection" and "connection reset by peer".
Laura: any recent config changes? deploy-bot, any autoscale events or infra deploys in last 10m?
deploy-bot: Deploy scale-note: service:edge-proxy v1.48.2 rolled at 08:05 UTC to eu-west-1 (canary 20% -> 100% completed 08:07). No infra autoscale events reported.
Daniel: hm canary finished right before spike. Let's verify if older instances still healthy.
Michelle: Running quick grep for 502 signature across backends: `kubectl logs -n prod deploy/edge-proxy --since=20m | grep 502 | head -n 50`
Michelle: sample log: `2023-08-01T08:12:23Z edge-proxy request_id=abc upstream=svc-user-profile:502 "GET /v1/profile" status=502 "upstream closed connection"`
Kira: user-profile seems to be the most common upstream returning 502. Checking its pods.
Kira: `kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=user-profile -o wide` -> several pods OOMKilled in the last 15m and rest are flapping.
Ryan: that fits: upstream instability -> gateway 502s. Any rollout touching user-profile or DB connections recently?
Laura: I see a jobs release for user-profile at 07:58 UTC (library patch). Could be related.
Daniel: Plan: 1) divert traffic away from failing user-profile instances (route around) 2) enable circuit-breaker / increase timeouts at edge-gw for user-profile path 3) scale user-profile and rollback last deploy if it looks correlated.
Michelle: Executing step 1: adding routing rule to blacklist unhealthy endpoints. `rbacctl route update edge-gw --remove-upstream user-profile-pod-3,user-profile-pod-4` -> done.
incident-bot: ACTION TAKEN: route update applied by Michelle at 08:20 UTC.
Kira: Enabling circuit breaker for user-profile on edge-gw policy: `edge-gwctl set-cb user-profile --consecutive-errors=5 --cooldown=30s` -> enabled.
Ryan: Scaling user-profile from 3 -> 8 replicas: `kubectl scale deploy user-profile --replicas=8 -n prod` -> scaling.
Laura: I'm watching pods come up, readiness is slow for some (DB migrations?). If new pods are healthy, we can gradually reintroduce traffic.
Michelle: CPU of user-profile pods before OOMs was ~600m with memory peaks before crash. Recent patch may have introduced memory leak.
Daniel: Decision: roll back user-profile to v1.73.1 (previous stable) to stop leak. Who can handle rollback?
Kira: I can cut a rollback. Performing `kubectl set image deploy/user-profile user-profile=registry/redwood/user-profile:v1.73.1 -n prod` -> started.
deploy-bot: Rollback triggered by Kira: user-profile -> v1.73.1. Rollback status: in progress.
Ryan: After routing change + cb + scaling, error rate dropped to 6% in 5m window. Good improvement.
Michelle: after rollback completion: new pods running v1.73.1, memory stable so far. Observability: errors down to 1.2% over last 10m.
Daniel: Customer impact: brief degradation between 08:12-08:28 UTC. Affected requests primarily profile reads; estimated 1.8k failed requests total, degraded for ~16 minutes. Escalate to CS for notice.
Laura: Noting action items: postmortem owner = Kira, root cause hypothesis = bad user-profile release causing memory pressure -> crash -> upstream 502s. Need better canary thresholds for memory.
Kira: I'll open an incident ticket and start a write-up. PID:INC-2023-482
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (route update, circuit-breaker, scale, rollback). Error rate returned to baseline at 08:28 UTC. Monitoring will keep 30m watch.
Daniel: Handoff to follow-up shift: @Ryan will own monitoring for next 2 hours and escalate if spike reappears. @Michelle can you coordinate comms to CS and update status page?
Michelle: Yep, paging CS and posting a status page update: "Partial degradation for profile reads 08:12–08:28 UTC. Root cause under investigation." :white_check_mark:
Ryan: I'll keep a pod-level watch and run a leak detection job across user-profile images.
Laura: Postmortem due EOD. Please include timeline, metrics, deploy diff and canary configs.
Kira: Capture logs & dumps: `kubectl get events --namespace prod --selector app=user-profile --since=1h > /tmp/user-profile-events.log` and upload to incident ticket.
Daniel: Good work team. If anything flares I'll re-open channel. For now we circulate summary to stakeholders.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: mitigations successful, error rate returned to baseline. Closure conditions met at 08:28 UTC."
